question: Which current B bodies explain their behavior independently of product task orchestration?
procedure: Read each listed complete implementation, inspect named caller/provider bodies and search symbol references. This is a bounded review of 13 of the 49 compat C files, not a complete component audit or proof of runtime reachability.

rows.evidence: Calls native RtlDosPathNameToNtPathName_U without a modern relative-output structure; clears the caller's original output structure. No task lookup or outward provider.
rows.remaining: Historical necessity and selected original caller ABI remain governed by existing mirror evidence; no new equivalence test run.

rows.evidence: Combines the original low-bit handle predicate with GetConsoleMode and preserves LastError. No frontend selection or product protocol.

rows.decision: split native resource mechanics from product delivery; not independent today
rows.evidence: TLS binding dispatches Duplicate and Close to service_duplicate_resource/service_close_resource in src/ntsrv-exe/opennt/source/base_service.c. The latter resolve worker reservations, console-associated worker connections, stream receipts and parent/worker wait delivery. src/ntsrv-exe/opennt/include/base_server.h remaps NtDuplicateObject/NtClose to these B entrypoints for retained server code.
rows.state: Borrowed synchronous resource scope; prior TLS binding is restored by the F dispatch caller. Local unbound duplicate allows only current-process resources.
rows.migration: Keep handle operations with explicit resolved resources in B; retain authenticated reservation/recipient selection and request wait policy in F. Redesign the retained C operation boundary before replacing this dispatch. Simply moving provider bodies to B or using raw cross-process handles is rejected.
rows.remaining: Trace each retained C request operation, delivery and failure unwind to design an explicit non-callback execution boundary. Two additional source-resolved F callback slots, not new approved exceptions or closed ledger IDs.

rows.evidence: Owns bounded DOS/WOW command strings and borrowed immutable TLS configuration; no lookup or request selection. worker_registry.c selects product paths and binary kind, binds the configuration around BaseGetVdmConfigInfo, then restores the previous binding.
rows.contract: Caller retains configuration lifetime; preserve capacity failures and original reservation value. Do not migrate worker selection into this unit.

rows.decision: retain B native console cell-grid mechanics
rows.evidence: Reads and writes the supplied console handle, copies/clips cells on resize, frees temporary buffers and propagates incomplete transfer failure. No NTCON transport or session lookup.
demsrch.c captures and searches a filename/index hint using an explicit directory handle and native NtQueryDirectoryFile. No task or CPU state is consulted.
rows.contract: Preserve native enumeration status and caller-owned buffer lifetime. This review is ownership evidence, not a new proof of directory mutation semantics.

rows.decision: retain B explicit invariant failure primitive
rows.evidence: virtual.c supplies an invalid instance identifier. The function constructs a noncontinuable failure record and invokes native fail-fast; it does not select a task, cancel a session or complete a request.
rows.contract: Do not replace with session cancellation or a returning failure. Runtime fault behavior was not rerun.

rows.decision: no outward implementation; retained no-op requires separate necessity evidence
rows.evidence: Body is empty; references occur in nt_eoi.c and nt_unix.c. It does not delegate to a product scheduler.
rows.remaining: Symbol references and the ownership comment do not prove original idle semantics equivalent. Reconcile selected call paths and original responsibility before changing or claiming full semantic review.

rows.decision: no outward implementation; explicit unavailable ABI providers
rows.evidence: EDL_fast_bop, c_VirtualiseInstruction and c_sas_touch invoke __debugbreak; the latter two return zero if execution continues. C c_main.c references the BOP symbol; sascdef.c references the SAS entries.
rows.remaining: Do not describe debugbreak as guaranteed termination or restore unsupported machine algorithms into B. Selected vector reachability and historical unavailable-provider semantics still need reconciliation.

rows.decision: retain B bounded input metadata mechanism
rows.evidence: Uses caller-owned counters, ring metadata and opaque numeric receipts. C nt_event.c/keyba.c maintain hardware history; F console_compat.c stages and consumes receipts. B never resolves a receipt to a task or frontend.
rows.contract: Original keyboard lock must cover tags and device state; preserve overwritten-slot rejection and selected ages across reset. No second input or session state machine.

rows.decision: retain B native wait resource with explicit outer lifetime
rows.evidence: Owns one auto-reset event, signal/wait/create/close only. C c_main.c waits/signals; F mvdm_standalone_worker.c starts it before host execution and ends it after producer shutdown.
rows.contract: The single-execution-thread and stopped-producer lifetime is a caller precondition, not internally synchronized teardown. Do not convert it to a scheduler or claim concurrent close safe.

rows.decision: native join mechanics with lifecycle contract needing clarification
rows.evidence: For a started thread, duplicates a synchronization handle, alerts the original handle, waits and closes the duplicate. For !started returns success without starting or joining the suspended thread. C nt_remove_event_thread supplies nt_init_called and ignores the result.
rows.remaining: Document/resolve the unstarted-thread process-exit policy and retained handle ownership at C/F teardown before calling this a generic join. No behavior change or bug assertion from source inspection alone.

rows.decision: retain B explicit unavailable native-service boundary
rows.evidence: Returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every request and owns no task state or callback. This does not implement hardware VDM monitoring.
rows.remaining: Callers must retain their existing unsupported-service behavior; this file alone does not prove every caller handles that status.

validation: Read-only source inspection; no new build, runtime test or publication. Full four-component migration ledger remains incomplete.
